intro: Crossing a land border in East Africa is usually straightforward if you prepare. Have your passport, visa or travel authorisation and yellow fever certificate ready, and expect it to take anywhere from ~30 minutes to a few hours, depending on queues. Long-distance bus companies stop at the border and wait while passengers go through immigration on both sides.
eac: The East African Community (EAC) is a regional bloc of eight partner states: Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (joined 2023), Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia (joined 2024), South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.
Ethiopia, Djibouti and Eritrea are not EAC members, so EAC arrangements do not apply when you cross into or out of them.

For citizens of EAC partner states, the EAC makes travel easier: in many cases they can cross with a national ID or an East African passport instead of a full passport, and stay for a while without a visa.
For visitors from outside the region, EAC membership does not mean visa-free travel. Each country still sets its own visa or entry rules, and you normally need separate permission for each one.
Many busy border posts have been rebuilt as One Stop Border Posts, where both countries' officials work in the same place, so you clear exit and entry together.
eatv: The East Africa Tourist Visa (EATV) is a single tourist visa covering Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. It allows multiple entries between those three countries, lasts ~90 days and has cost ~US$100.
You usually apply through the immigration service of the country you will enter first, and you must enter that country first.
If you leave the three-country area (for example, into Tanzania), the EATV generally ends, and you need a new visa to come back in.

Kenya replaced most visas with an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) in January 2024, and later exempted many African nationals from it. Public guidance on how the EATV fits with Kenya's eTA is unclear, so check the official Kenyan, Ugandan and Rwandan immigration sites before relying on it.
Tanzania, Burundi, South Sudan, Ethiopia and the other countries in this guide are not part of the EATV.
prepare: Make sure your passport is valid for at least ~6 months beyond your travel dates and has a few blank pages.
Bring your yellow fever vaccination certificate. It is often checked at land borders, especially if you are arriving from a country with yellow fever risk. Carry the original.
Get your visa, e-visa or eTA online before you travel where you can. Do not count on buying one at the border.
Carry some US dollars in clean, recent notes for any fees, plus a little local currency for the other side.
If you are on a long-distance bus, the company handles the stop: get off, clear exit, walk across, clear entry and get back on your bus. Keep your ticket and remember your bus and seat number.
Keep every receipt for visa or fee payments until you have left the country.
Do not change money with touts at the border. Rates are often poor and short-changing is common. Use a bank, a licensed bureau, an ATM or mobile money on the other side.
Do not carry packages for strangers, and do not photograph border buildings or officials.
